claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
Mo is added to the alloy composition.
Added Mo partitions to the matrix.
Mo partitioning to the matrix causes solid-solution strengthening.
The larger atomic size of Mo distorts the alloy lattice.
Mo-induced lattice distortion impedes dislocation movement.
The Mo lattice-obstacle mechanism provides particle strengthening similar to that in nickel-based superalloys.
Mo addition can preserve toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading.
The applicable treatment is exposure at 700 °C for 1000 hours followed by room-temperature tensile testing.
The Mo-containing alloy will have greater toughness than the alloy without Mo under otherwise identical conditions.
The Mo-containing alloy will have greater strength than the alloy without Mo under otherwise identical conditions.
The predicted improvement applies at both room and high temperatures.
The baseline alloy without Mo is a single-phase solid solution.
Comparing Mo-containing and Mo-free alloys after the same exposure and tensile test can test the hypothesis.
Failure of the Mo-containing alloy to improve both toughness and strength relative to the Mo-free alloy would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted strength improvement conflicts with the cited Mo-alloy observation: the Mo-containing alloy had lower ultimate tensile strength and the worst behavior among the directionally solidified samples between 600 and 800 °C.
The hypothesis specifies a single-phase solid-solution alloy, whereas the cited systems contain coherent γ′ precipitates and, potentially, a Heusler phase.

The mediator describes solid-solution strengthening by matrix-solute Mo, but the mechanism then labels this as particle strengthening. The cited particle-strengthening mechanism instead arises from discrete coherent γ′ precipitates.
The defined loading regime contains only room-temperature tensile testing, while the predicted outcome additionally claims improvement at high temperatures.
